mainTopic: Whether היתר joins איסור to make a כזית, and רב דימי's defense that a כזית בכדי אכילת פרס is Torah law, against אביי's challenges from the טבול יום soup, כותח הבבלי, and the ברייתות of mixed תרומה.
overview: This amud opens by agreeing that the rule היתר מצטרף לאיסור, learned from the פסוק about leaven on the מזבח, also applies to חמץ on פסח. It adds that this rule rejects אביי's view that offering less than a כזית counts as a הקטרה. Then רב דימי teaches that in all other Torah prohibitions היתר does not join איסור, except for a נזיר. אביי challenges him from a משנה about a חולין soup with תרומה spices that was touched by a טבול יום. A זר is lashed for a כזית of that soup, which seems to show that היתר joins איסור. רב דימי answers that the lashes come from eating a כזית of the תרומה itself within כדי אכילת פרס, which he holds is Torah law. He defends this against a question from כותח הבבלי. He also answers two ברייתות about mixed-up pots and baskets by explaining that each case involves only rabbinic תרומה. Finally the גמרא asks whether the word מִשְׁרַת in the נזיר פסוק is really free to teach this rule, and the ברייתא it starts quoting continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Does the joining rule also apply to חמץ on פסח?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes the earlier teaching further: if היתר joins איסור for offering leaven on the מזבח, it should also join for eating חמץ on פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: [If so,] regarding חמץ on פסח too [a permitted substance should join a forbidden one].
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of a question that began on the previous amud. The גמרא asks whether the rule just learned for offering leaven on the מזבח also applies to eating חמץ on פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule היתר מצטרף לאיסור was learned from a פסוק about offerings on the מזבח. The question is whether it extends to the eating prohibition of חמץ on פסח. If it does, that would be a big expansion, since normally היתר does not join איסור.

keyTerms.meaning: regarding, with respect to
leavened food on פסח
also, too

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The words 'אי הכי' ('if so') and the earlier discussion of the פסוק about leaven on the מזבח come right before this line.

phrases.english: With regard to חמץ on Pesach also [should permitted join forbidden]?
phrases.notes: This finishes a question that started on the previous amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעִנְיַן חָמֵץ בַּפֶּסַח נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the question on the previous amud boundary about the scope of the rule derived from the מזבח פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The scope of the derivation that היתר מצטרף לאיסור for offering leaven on the מזבח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the rule comes from the same kind of wording, it should apply to eating חמץ on פסח too. That would make the rule broader than expected.

steps.title: Yes, and it rejects אביי's view on less than a כזית
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the point and adds that the teaching also rejects אביי's view that offering less than a כזית counts as a הקטרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, indeed it is so. And [the teaching] comes to exclude the view of אביי, who said that offering less than a כזית counts as an offering. It teaches us that an offering is not less than a כזית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by agreeing: yes, the rule applies to חמץ on פסח too. It then explains what the teaching adds for the מזבח: it rejects אביי's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי held that putting even less than a כזית of leaven on the מזבח is a punishable הקטרה. The teaching shows that the permitted part must join to reach a full כזית before there is liability. That means a הקטרה of less than a כזית does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: yes, indeed it is so
to exclude, to reject (another view)
burning an offering on the מזבח
an olive-sized amount, the standard minimum
it teaches us

steps.whyThisMatters: It establishes that the כזית minimum applies to הקטרה on the מזבח, not only to eating.

phrases.english: Yes, indeed it is so.
And [it comes] to exclude [the view] of Abaye, who said:
There is [a valid] offering for less than an olive-bulk,
it teaches us that an offering
is not [counted] for less than an olive-bulk.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין הָכִי נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 1 by agreeing and adding a further purpose of the teaching.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Concession plus a new purpose: the questioner is right, and the source also teaches something else.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might have thought, like אביי, that any amount of leaven placed on the מזבח is a punishable הקטרה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule does apply to חמץ on פסח, and a הקטרה requires a full כזית.

steps.title: רב דימי repeats the general rule
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי sits and teaches the rule that in all איסורין, היתר does not join איסור, except for a נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי sat and was saying this teaching.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line that opens a new discussion. רב דימי repeats the earlier rule (from רבי יוחנן) that היתר does not join איסור, except for נזיר, and this prepares the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'This teaching' refers to the rule stated earlier in the סוגיא. The rule is that in all Torah prohibitions a permitted substance does not combine with a forbidden one to reach a כזית. The only exception is the איסורי נזיר.

keyTerms.meaning: sat (and was teaching)
a teaching, a halachic statement

phrases.english: Rav Dimi sat
and was stating this teaching.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַב דִּימִי וְקָאָמַר לַהּ לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the חמץ discussion to a new exchange about the general rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In all Torah prohibitions, היתר does not join איסור, except for the איסורי נזיר.

steps.title: אביי questions the general rule
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב דימי whether it is really true that in all other prohibitions, היתר never joins איסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב דימי: And in all other prohibitions in the Torah, does a permitted substance not join a forbidden one?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins a challenge against רב דימי's rule. His question sounds like a request for information, but it is really a challenge, and he brings his proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי doubts that נזיר is the only case where היתר joins איסור. He is about to show a case elsewhere where a permitted food takes on the status of the forbidden food mixed with it.

keyTerms.meaning: the prohibitions of the Torah
a permitted substance joins a forbidden one (to reach the minimum amount)

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Dimi:
And with regard to all prohibitions in the Torah,
a permitted substance does not join a forbidden one?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי לְרַב דִּימִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly challenges the rule רב דימי stated in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that only נזיר is an exception to the rule that היתר does not join איסור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If another area of halacha shows permitted food taking on the status of the forbidden food, the rule cannot be as absolute as רב דימי says.

steps.title: The proof: a תרומה soup touched by a טבול יום
steps.stepSummary: אביי cites a משנה: if the soup is תרומה and the garlic and oil are חולין, a טבול יום's touch disqualifies everything. If the soup is חולין and only the garlic and oil are תרומה, only the spot he touched is disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in a משנה: A thick soup of תרומה, with garlic and oil of חולין, that a טבול יום touched part of, he disqualified all of it. A thick soup of חולין, with garlic and oil of תרומה, that a טבול יום touched part of, he disqualified only the place he touched.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי quotes a משנה as the basis for his challenge. His proof will come from the second case, where the soup is חולין and only the garlic and oil are תרומה. The next steps (6–8) build the proof from that case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טבול יום disqualifies תרומה by touching it, but not חולין. In the first case, the חולין garlic and oil are secondary to the main תרומה soup, so the whole pot is disqualified. In the second case, the main dish is חולין, yet the spot he touched is still disqualified. That second ruling is the one אביי will use against רב דימי.

keyTerms.meaning: a thick soup or stew
the holy portion given to a כהן
ordinary, non-holy food
someone who immersed today but is not fully pure until nightfall
disqualified (made unfit)

steps.confusionAlert: A טבול יום does not make food טמא in the usual sense. He only makes תרומה פסול (unfit), and he has no effect on חולין. That is why it matters so much whether the garlic and oil count as תרומה.
steps.whyThisMatters: The second case raises a puzzle: the small amount of תרומה should be cancelled by the majority of חולין, yet the touched spot is disqualified. The explanation of that puzzle becomes אביי's proof against רב דימי.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn: A thick soup of teruma
with the garlic and the oil of non-sacred produce,
and a tevul yom touched part of them,
he disqualified all of them.
A thick soup of non-sacred produce
with the garlic and the oil of teruma,
and a tevul yom touched part of them,
he disqualified only
the place that he touched.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind אביי's challenge in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That היתר can join or take on the status of איסור outside of נזיר, against רב דימי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a חולין soup with תרומה garlic and oil touched by a טבול יום, where the touched spot is disqualified even though the spices should be nullified by the majority.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי's challenge rests on the second case of the משנה. There, the soup is mostly חולין, yet the spot touched by the טבול יום is disqualified. The next steps explain why, and that explanation becomes the proof that היתר joins איסור outside of נזיר.

steps.title: Why is the touched spot disqualified if the spices are cancelled?
steps.stepSummary: אביי recalls an earlier discussion that asked why the touched spot becomes disqualified, since the תרומה spices should be cancelled by the majority of חולין soup.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we discussed this: Why is the spot he touched disqualified? The spices should be cancelled out by the majority!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי is still building his proof. He brings up an old question about the משנה's second case, where the soup is חולין and only the spices are תרומה. This question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The spices of תרומה are a small part of a mostly חולין soup. Normally a minority gets cancelled (בטל ברוב), so the spices should count as plain חולין. If that were true, a טבול יום touching them should disqualify nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: And we discussed it (we raised a question on it)
The spot that he touched
Spices (here: the garlic and oil)
Cancelled out by the majority

phrases.english: And we discussed it:
Why is the place he touched disqualified?
But the spices are cancelled out in the majority!
phrases.notes: The חולין soup is the majority.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָוֵינַן בַּהּ: מְקוֹם מַגָּעוֹ אַמַּאי פְּסוּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a question on the second case of the משנה that אביי cited in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why are the spices not cancelled by the majority of חולין soup?

steps.title: Because a non-כהן gets lashes for a כזית
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה answers that the spices keep their status because a זר is lashed for eating a כזית of the mixture.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה בר בר חנה said: What is the reason? Because a non-כהן gets lashes for eating a כזית of them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר בר חנה answers the question from step 6. The spices are not cancelled, because the Torah still treats the mixture as real תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a זר is punished with lashes for eating a כזית of the mixture, then the תרומה inside it was clearly not cancelled. That is why a טבול יום's touch still disqualifies the spot he touched.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, because
A non-כהן, who may not eat תרומה
Gets lashes (מלקות)
An olive-size amount, the minimum for punishment

phrases.english: And Rabba bar bar Chana said:
What is the reason —
since a non-priest is lashed for them for an olive-bulk.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה: מַה טַּעַם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The spices are not cancelled, since a זר is lashed for eating a כזית of the mixture.

steps.title: אביי concludes: so היתר must join איסור
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that lashes for a כזית of the mixture only make sense if the permitted soup joins the forbidden spices to make up the כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? Is it not because the permitted food joins the forbidden food?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his proof against רב דימי. He says the only way a זר gets lashes here is if the חולין soup counts together with the תרומה to make the כזית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תרומה spices alone are less than a כזית in each bite. So the full כזית must be partly חולין. That is היתר joining איסור, in a case that has nothing to do with נזיר, against רב דימי's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How does it work?
Is it not because…
Joins together, combines

phrases.english: What are the circumstances,
is it not because the permitted joins with the forbidden?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי, לָאו מִשּׁוּם דְּהֶיתֵּר מִצְטָרֵף לְאִיסּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from רבה בר בר חנה's answer and turns it into a proof against רב דימי.
steps.raayaObject: That היתר joins איסור even outside of נזיר, against רב דימי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The טבול יום soup משנה together with רבה בר בר חנה's explanation that a זר is lashed for a כזית.

steps.title: רב דימי: the כזית is eaten within כדי אכילת פרס
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי rejects the proof. The case is one where there is enough תרומה that a person eats a full כזית of it within the time of eating a half-loaf.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. What does 'a כזית' mean? That there is a כזית of תרומה within the time it takes to eat a half-loaf.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי pushes back against אביי's proof. He says the כזית is made of real תרומה alone, so no חולין needs to join it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating small bits over a short time counts as one eating. If the person eats enough of the mixture to swallow a full כזית of pure תרומה within כדי אכילת פרס, he is lashed for the תרומה itself. The חולין is not counted at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Half a loaf of bread
The time it takes to eat half a loaf. Eating within this time counts as one eating.

steps.confusionAlert: רב דימי is NOT saying a person eats a כזית of the mixture. He means a person eats a full כזית of the תרומה part alone, spread out within the time of כדי אכילת פרס.

phrases.english: No, what is meant by an olive-bulk —
that there is an olive-bulk within the time of eating a half-loaf.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, מַאי כְּזַיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's proof by explaining the case another way.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the משנה proves היתר joins איסור.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The lashes can come from a full כזית of pure תרומה eaten within כדי אכילת פרס. No joining of היתר is needed.

steps.title: Is כזית בכדי אכילת פרס a Torah law?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks whether eating a כזית within כדי אכילת פרס is truly a Torah-level rule that brings lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is a כזית within the time of eating a half-loaf a Torah law?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי checks the basis of רב דימי's answer. Lashes are a Torah punishment, so רב דימי's answer only works if this rule is from the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If כזית בכדי אכילת פרס were only a rabbinic rule, it could not explain why a זר gets Torah lashes. רב דימי's answer depends on it being Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: From the Torah (Torah-level law)

phrases.english: And an olive-bulk within the time of eating a half-loaf —
is it a Torah law?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְזַיִת בִּכְדֵי אֲכִילַת פְּרָס דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the basis of רב דימי's answer in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether כזית בכדי אכילת פרס brings a Torah-level punishment.

steps.title: רב דימי: Yes, it is Torah law
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי answers that כזית בכדי אכילת פרס is indeed a Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי gives a short answer: yes, it is from the Torah. This answer sets up אביי's next challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By saying yes, רב דימי keeps his answer to the soup case. But he now has to accept everything that follows from this rule, and אביי uses that next.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question from step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: כזית בכדי אכילת פרס is a Torah-level law.

steps.title: Then why do the רבנן argue about כותח הבבלי?
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב דימי: if כזית בכדי אכילת פרס is Torah law, why do the רבנן disagree with רבי אליעזר and say there is no Torah punishment for כותח הבבלי on פסח?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why do the רבנן disagree with רבי אליעזר about Babylonian כותח?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב דימי's yes answer. He points to a known מחלוקת about כותח הבבלי, a dip that contains some flour (חמץ).
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that a person is punished for eating a mixture that contains חמץ, and the רבנן disagree. But if eating a כזית בכדי אכילת פרס is Torah law, even the רבנן should agree there is punishment when someone eats enough כותח to swallow a כזית of חמץ in that time. So why do they argue at all?

keyTerms.meaning: If so
They disagree
Babylonian כותח, a dip made with some bread or flour, so it contains חמץ

steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge ties the soup case back to חמץ on פסח, the main topic of the סוגיא. It tests whether רב דימי's idea of כזית בכדי אכילת פרס can stand.

phrases.english: If so,
why do the Rabbis disagree
with Rabbi Eliezer
regarding Babylonian kutach?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אַמַּאי פְּלִיגִי רַבָּנַן עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּכוּתָּח הַבַּבְלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רב דימי's yes answer from step 11 to raise a new problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי's claim that כזית בכדי אכילת פרס is a Torah law.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If it were Torah law, the רבנן would have to agree with רבי אליעזר that one is punished for eating כותח when a כזית of חמץ is eaten within כדי אכילת פרס. But they disagree.

steps.title: רב דימי turns the question back on אביי
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי argues that אביי's own explanation, היתר מצטרף לאיסור, faces the same problem with כותח הבבלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what will you say? That the permitted food joins the forbidden food? In the end, the same question remains: why do the רבנן disagree with רבי אליעזר about כותח הבבלי?
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי does not answer the question yet. He first shows that אביי's alternative explanation has exactly the same problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If permitted food joined forbidden food to make a כזית, then כותח should surely bring a Torah punishment. So the disagreement of the רבנן with רבי אליעזר is a difficulty for both views. Since the question hits both sides, it cannot be used to reject רב דימי alone.

keyTerms.meaning: Permitted food joins with forbidden food to make up the required amount
In the end; the problem still remains
A Babylonian dip made with bread crusts (חמץ), milk, and salt

phrases.english: Rather, what [will you say]?
Because the permitted joins with the forbidden?
In the end
why do the Rabbis disagree
with Rabbi Eliezer about Babylonian kutach?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַאי, מִשּׁוּם דְּהֶיתֵּר מִצְטָרֵף לְאִיסּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to אביי's challenge in step 12 by showing that it applies equally to אביי's own view.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's alternative explanation that היתר מצטרף לאיסור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If permitted food joins forbidden food, כותח הבבלי should certainly bring a Torah punishment. So why do the רבנן exempt it?

steps.title: Why כותח הבבלי is different
steps.stepSummary: כותח is exempt because, in practice, no one eats a כזית of its חמץ within כדי אכילת פרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, set aside כותח הבבלי, because it never has a כזית within the time of eating a half-loaf. If someone eats it plain, swallowing it by itself, his behavior is ignored because no normal person eats that way. And if he dips food into it, he does not eat a כזית within כדי אכילת פרס.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי gives the real reason the רבנן exempt כותח. It has nothing to do with whether כזית בכדי אכילת פרס is a Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are only two ways to eat כותח. Eating it plain is so unusual that the law ignores it. Dipping uses so little of it that you never reach a כזית of חמץ within כדי אכילת פרס. So the רבנן can agree that the rule is Torah law and still exempt כותח.

keyTerms.meaning: Set aside; that case is different
The time it takes to eat a half-loaf of bread
His unusual behavior is ignored compared with normal people
Dipping food into the כותח

steps.whyThisMatters: This removes the difficulty from step 12. The dispute about כותח depends on how it is actually eaten, not on whether the rule is from the Torah.

phrases.english: Rather: leave aside Babylonian kutach

phrases.aramaic: דְּלֵית בֵּיהּ כְּזַיִת בִּכְדֵי אֲכִילַת פְּרָס.
phrases.english: since it has no olive-bulk within the time of eating a half-loaf.
If he swallows it plain and eats it,
his intent is nullified compared with all people.
And if he dips [food] and eats —

phrases.aramaic: לֵית בֵּיהּ כְּזַיִת בִּכְדֵי אֲכִילַת פְּרָס.
phrases.english: there is no olive-bulk in it within the time of eating a half-loaf.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: הַנַּח לְכוּתָּח הַבַּבְלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the positive answer after step 13 showed that the question applies to both sides.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the realistic way כותח is eaten never reaches the amount.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן exempt כותח because they hold that כזית בכדי אכילת פרס is not Torah law.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן exempt כותח because a כזית of its חמץ is never eaten within כדי אכילת פרס in any normal way.

steps.title: אביי quotes the ברייתא of the two pots and two mortars
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a ברייתא. There are pots and mortars of חולין and of תרומה, the mortars' contents fall in, and we do not know which fell where. Everything is permitted because of שאני אומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי objected: There are two pots, one of חולין and one of תרומה. In front of them are two mortars, one of חולין and one of תרומה. These fell into those, and everything is permitted. For I say: the תרומה fell into the תרומה, and the חולין fell into the חולין.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a ברייתא to challenge רב דימי. This step only quotes the source; the challenge itself is spelled out in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is lenient in a case of doubt. It assumes the best case, that each kind fell into its matching pot. That way the pot of חולין stays permitted to a non-כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: A mortar used for crushing spices
'For I say': in a doubt, we assume the lenient explanation
Ordinary, non-sacred produce

phrases.english: He objected: two pots,

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת שֶׁל חוּלִּין וְאַחַת שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה,
phrases.english: one of non-sacred produce and one of teruma,
and in front of them two mortars,

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת שֶׁל חוּלִּין וְאַחַת שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה,
phrases.english: one of non-sacred produce and one of teruma,
and these fell into those — they are permitted.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֲנִי אוֹמֵר: תְּרוּמָה לְתוֹךְ הַתְּרוּמָה נָפְלָה,
phrases.english: For I say: the teruma fell into the teruma,
and the non-sacred fell into the non-sacred.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: שְׁתֵּי קְדֵירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new attack on רב דימי's claim in step 11, using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי's claim that כזית בכדי אכילת פרס is Torah law
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup: the ברייתא is lenient in a doubt. The next step will show why that is a problem.

steps.title: Why the pots baraita contradicts רב דימי
steps.stepSummary: If כזית בכדי אכילת פרס is Torah law, eating from the pot might be a Torah prohibition. So how can we rely on שאני אומר?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that a כזית within כדי אכילת פרס is Torah law, why do we say, 'For I say the תרומה fell into the תרומה,' and so on?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי now spells out his challenge from the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose the תרומה actually fell into the pot of חולין. Then a non-כהן eating from it would eat a כזית of תרומה within כדי אכילת פרס. According to רב דימי, that would be a Torah prohibition, and we would not normally rely on a lenient assumption like שאני אומר to permit a possible Torah prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say (introduces the opponent's position to show its problem)
A law from the Torah itself
Why do we say?

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ כְּזַיִת בִּכְדֵי אֲכִילַת פְּרָס דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא,
phrases.english: And if you say an olive-bulk within the time of eating a half-loaf is Torah law,
why do we say
'For I say the teruma [fell] into, etc.'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ כְּזַיִת בִּכְדֵי אֲכִילַת פְּרָס דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the challenge contained in the ברייתא quoted in step 15.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being lenient in a doubt fits a rabbinic prohibition, not a Torah one. So the ברייתא implies that כזית בכדי אכילת פרס is not Torah law.

steps.title: Spice teruma is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי answers that the pots ברייתא is about spices, and תרומה from spices is only דרבנן, so leniency is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Set aside תרומת תבלין, which is only דרבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי answers אביי's challenge by pointing out that the case in the ברייתא is about spices.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mortars are used for crushing spices. By Torah law, תרומה is required only from grain, wine, and oil. תרומה from spices is a rabbinic rule, so the חכמים could be lenient with שאני אומר without affecting the Torah status of כזית בכדי אכילת פרס.

keyTerms.meaning: תרומה separated from spices
A rule made by the חכמים, not from the Torah

phrases.english: He said to him:
Leave aside spice teruma, which is rabbinic.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הַנַּח לִתְרוּמַת תַּבְלִין דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to a rabbinic-level case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא shows that we are lenient even about a possible Torah-level כזית בכדי אכילת פרס.
steps.terutzMaskana: The leniency applies only because spice תרומה is rabbinic.

steps.title: אביי quotes the ברייתא of two baskets and two סאה vessels
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a second ברייתא with the same leniency, this time about baskets and סאה measures of produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: He objected again: There are two baskets, one of חולין and one of תרומה. In front of them are two סאה measures, one of חולין and one of תרומה. These fell into those, and they are permitted. For I say: the חולין fell into the חולין, and the תרומה fell into the תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a second ברייתא to challenge רב דימי again. This step quotes the source, and the next step states the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Baskets and סאה measures hold grain, not spices. תרומה from grain is required by the Torah. So רב דימי's previous answer, that the case is only rabbinic, does not work here.

keyTerms.meaning: A basket
A large measuring vessel for produce

steps.confusionAlert: This looks like a repeat of the pots ברייתא, but the key change is the produce. These are grain containers, so this is Torah-level תרומה, not rabbinic spice תרומה.

phrases.english: He objected: two baskets,

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת שֶׁל חוּלִּין וְאַחַת שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה,
phrases.english: one of non-sacred produce and one of teruma,
and in front of them two se'ah measures,

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת שֶׁל חוּלִּין וְאַחַת שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה,
phrases.english: one of non-sacred produce and one of teruma,
and these fell into those — they are permitted,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֲנִי אוֹמֵר: חוּלִּין לְתוֹךְ חוּלִּין נָפְלוּ,
phrases.english: for I say: the non-sacred fell into the non-sacred,
the teruma fell into the teruma.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: שְׁתֵּי קוּפּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel ברייתא that avoids רב דימי's answer in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי's claim that כזית בכדי אכילת פרס is Torah law, and his spice answer in step 17
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup: the same leniency appears in a case of grain תרומה, which is Torah-level.

steps.title: The challenge returns for Torah-level teruma
steps.stepSummary: With grain תרומה from the Torah, אביי asks again how we can rely on שאני אומר if כזית בכדי אכילת פרס is Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that a כזית within כדי אכילת פרס is Torah law, why do we say, 'For I say'?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי repeats his challenge with a case of grain תרומה, so the spice answer from step 17 cannot help. The next step gives רב דימי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grain תרומה is Torah-level. If the תרומה fell into the חולין, eating it would mean eating a כזית of תרומה within כדי אכילת פרס, which רב דימי calls a Torah prohibition. Yet the ברייתא is still lenient, which seems to show the rule is not from the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: תרומה from grain, which the Torah requires

steps.whatToRemember: אביי keeps testing רב דימי's view that כזית בכדי אכילת פרס is Torah law against cases where we are lenient with שאני אומר. The spice answer worked for the pots, but the grain case brings the challenge back.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ כְּזַיִת בִּכְדֵי אֲכִילַת פְּרָס דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא —
phrases.english: And if you say an olive-bulk within the time of eating a half-loaf is Torah law —
why do we say 'For I say'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ כְּזַיִת בִּכְדֵי אֲכִילַת פְּרָס דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא — אַמַּאי אָמְרִינַן ״שֶׁאֲנִי אוֹמֵר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the challenge from the ברייתא in step 18.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A lenient assumption in a doubt should not permit a possible Torah prohibition. Since the ברייתא is lenient even with Torah-level תרומה, it implies that כזית בכדי אכילת פרס is not Torah law.

steps.title: Teruma today is only rabbinic, so leniency is allowed
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי answers that the baskets ברייתא deals with תרומה in our times, which is only דרבנן. So relying on שאני אומר is fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: He (רב דימי) said to him (אביי): Leave aside תרומה nowadays, because it is only דרבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי answers אביי's challenge about the baskets of grain. He says that even grain תרומה today is only a rabbinic law, so the ברייתא can be lenient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי thought grain תרומה is from the Torah, so eating a doubtful mixture might break Torah law if כזית בכדי אכילת פרס is Torah law. רב דימי answers that since the Jewish people left the land, תרומה is only דרבנן. With a rabbinic prohibition, we are allowed to be lenient with שאני אומר, so the question goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: Leave aside. Here it means: don't bring a proof from this case.
תרומה in our times, after the exile, when the Torah-level obligation no longer applies
Rabbinic law, not Torah law

steps.whatToRemember: Both of אביי's ברייתות are answered the same way. Each case involves only a rabbinic prohibition: spices in the first, and תרומה today in the second. So neither ברייתא proves that כזית בכדי אכילת פרס is not Torah law.
steps.confusionAlert: רב דימי is not saying grain תרומה was never from the Torah. He is saying that the ברייתא is talking about our times, when תרומה is only דרבנן.

phrases.english: He said to him: Leave aside teruma
in our times, which is rabbinic.
phrases.notes: After the exile, תרומה is only a rabbinic obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הַנַּח לִתְרוּמָה בַּזְּמַן הַזֶּה דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 19 by placing the ברייתא in our times, the same way Step 17 answered the first ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the prohibition in the ברייתא is only rabbinic.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Grain תרומה is from the Torah, so leniency would risk a Torah prohibition.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about תרומה today, which is דרבנן, so שאני אומר is allowed.

steps.title: Is the word מִשְׁרַת really free for this teaching?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the source for היתר מצטרף לאיסור by נזיר. The word מִשְׁרַת seems to be needed for a different teaching found in a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And does this word מִשְׁרַת come to teach this? That word is needed for what was taught in a ברייתא: "מִשְׁרַת" —
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the main source and asks whether the word מִשְׁרַת really teaches that a permitted food joins with a forbidden one. It begins quoting a ברייתא that uses the word for something else. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the word מִשְׁרַת ("soaked") was the Torah source that by נזיר, a permitted food combines with a forbidden one. Now the גמרא objects that a word already used for one teaching cannot automatically be used for another. The ברייתא starting here will show the other use, so the source is now in doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: "Soaking" of grapes. A word in the נזיר verse that serves as a source for a teaching.
A permitted food joins with a forbidden food to complete the amount needed for punishment
It is needed for, meaning the word is already used for another teaching
As was taught in a ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the law is wrong. It is only asking where the source is, since the word seems to be already taken.
steps.whyThisMatters: This question decides whether there is any Torah source for היתר מצטרף לאיסור by נזיר. It reopens the main סוגיא after the side discussion about כזית בכדי אכילת פרס.

phrases.english: And this word "soaked"
phrases.notes: This is the word in the נזיר verse used earlier as the source.

phrases.english: does it come for this?
phrases.notes: Meaning: to teach that permitted and forbidden foods combine.

phrases.english: This word is needed
phrases.notes: It is already used for a different teaching.

phrases.english: for what was taught in a baraita: "Soaked" —
phrases.notes: The ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַאי ״מִשְׁרַת״ לְהָכִי הוּא דַּאֲתָא? הַאי מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the כזית בכדי אכילת פרס discussion and goes back to challenging the source word מִשְׁרַת.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using מִשְׁרַת as the source for היתר מצטרף לאיסור by נזיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A word that a ברייתא already uses for another teaching is not free to teach this law as well.
